name: ANGELIQUE Ceramics Taller & Showroom
address: Calle 24 N # 5AN - 48, Barrio San Vicente, Cali
description: A ceramics studio and showroom in San Vicente making handmade tableware, with wheel and hand-building classes and a firing service for outside potters. The studio's highlights also show raku and obvara firing work.
descriptionOriginal: Clases de Cerámica / Torno Alfarero & Técnicas Manuales; servicio de quema bizcocho (900°C) y esmalte (1250°C).
details: The website lists an 'Experiencia Integral' (4 sessions, 8 hours, COP 550.000) and an 'Experiencia Parcial' (1 session, 2 hours, COP 175.000), with slots on Wednesday 9-11 and 18-20, Friday 9-11 and Saturday 9-11. The firing service (bisque 900°C, glaze 1250°C, two kilns of different sizes) is by appointment only: send photos of pieces, clay type and glazes by WhatsApp (+57 317 366 8120), and pieces must be bone-dry with glaze-free bases. Firing prices are in an image on the site and could not be read. Prices may have changed.

name: La Alfarería Cali
description: A pottery workshop in San Antonio that offers wheel and hand-building classes, creative workshops and handmade ceramics made to order. Classes can be taken one-to-one or in pairs.
descriptionOriginal: Clases de cerámica | Clases de torno | Venta cerámica artesanal. Clases y talleres creativos, pedidos personalizados. San Antonio, Cali.
details: September 2026 flyers advertise hand-building classes in packs of 2, 4 or 8 sessions on Thursdays and Sundays, and wheel classes Monday to Friday. Both can be taken one-to-one or in pairs, and you sign up by Instagram direct message. Its Google Maps listing (October 2026) gives the address as Carrera 5 # 2-08 and the phone as 304 251 3909; confirm by message before going. No prices were visible.

name: El Palomar Cerámicas
description: A family ceramics workshop and shop in San Antonio, known for its small clay doves (palomitas), horses, cats and figures of Cali street life. Pieces are decorated before firing and then glazed.
descriptionOriginal: "La arcilla llegó como una intuición a la familia de El Palomar." Hecho a mano desde 1973 en Cali.
details: The workshop is run by Isleny Valencia Gómez and her family, and it has a Colombia Artesanal profile on the Valle del Cauca route. Pieces include palomitas sold in pairs, 'caballos de la prosperidad', cats inspired by Hernando Tejada, religious figures made to order, and replicas of San Antonio's traditional macetas. Visits can be arranged ('Agenda tu visita') by phone (311 757 9898) or by email (elpalomar@ceramicaselpalomar.com). No classes are mentioned. The website ceramicaselpalomar.com did not load during verification.

name: Rosana Ocaña (Taller Arteser / Rao Cerámica)
description: A ceramics technologist with about 30 years of work in clay who teaches wheel, coil, slab and pinch techniques and fires in a gas kiln. She is known for her corn-cob ahumadoras (incense burners) and learned the paddling (paleteado) technique in Peru.
descriptionOriginal: Tecnóloga en cerámica. Habla de la arcilla como una materia viva y bondadosa, a la que hay que respetar y saber trabajar.
details: Her Colombia Artesanal profile (Taller Arteser, Ruta Valle del Cauca, last updated November 2024) says she and her husband, visual arts teacher Oscar Esteban Martínez, began teaching once they moved to Cali, and that many of her students later opened their own workshops. Her Instagram has 'clases' highlights, but no schedules or prices were visible. Contact: 318 326 2418 or rosanaceravitro@gmail.com.

name: Taller Cerámica Creativa
description: A long-running ceramics production workshop in Cali that makes traditional Colombian ceramic pieces such as napkin holders, candle holders and other decorative ware.
descriptionOriginal: Cerámicas tradicionales de Colombia. Más de 30 años de tradición artesanal.
details: This appears to be a production workshop. The profile does not mention classes, supplies or firing services. Contact is through a WhatsApp link on its Instagram. No street address was shown on the page that was verified.

name: Instituto Departamental de Bellas Artes – Maestro(a) en Artes Plásticas
nameEnglish: Bellas Artes Cali – Fine Arts degree
description: A public arts university in Cali whose Faculty of Visual and Applied Arts offers a ten-semester, accredited professional degree in plastic arts. Students work across two- and three-dimensional media, with an emphasis on research through making.
descriptionOriginal: Formar artistas-profesionales en artes plásticas con un reconocido énfasis investigativo-creativo, a través del conocimiento y dominio de diversos medios de expresión visual.
details: The degree is SNIES 1737: 160 credits over 10 semesters, in person, daytime, with high-quality accreditation (Resolución 013003 of 2023). Applications for 2027-1 are open from 5 October to 25 November 2026, with a registration fee of COP 123.400. The faculty also teaches Graphic Design. The programme page does not list a dedicated ceramics course.

name: Bellas Artes – Cursos de Extensión
description: Open-enrolment short courses at Bellas Artes for children, teenagers and adults, including artistic drawing in pencil and acrylic, figure drawing, painting and digital graphic design, alongside music courses.
descriptionOriginal: Cursos de Extensión – Periodo 2026-3. Inscripciones abiertas: septiembre de 2026.
details: You register through an online form and pay by bank transfer, PSE or at the Tesorería. Groups open only once the minimum enrolment is reached, and the start date is sent by email. Schedules and fees are published per course. Contact: apoyo.educacioncontinua@bellasartes.edu.co. No ceramics course appears in the 2026-3 offer. The institution also runs a Diplomado en educación artística (COP 1.650.000 for the general public).

name: Universidad del Valle – Licenciatura en Artes Visuales (Departamento de Artes Visuales y Estética)
nameEnglish: Universidad del Valle – Visual Arts degree
address: Ciudad Universitaria Meléndez, Edificio E10, Espacio 2026, Cali
description: The public university's visual arts department offers a ten-semester Licenciatura in Visual Arts that combines studio practice in drawing and project workshops with art theory and teacher training. The Faculty of Integrated Arts also runs Industrial Design and Graphic Design programmes.
descriptionOriginal: Formación académica y desarrollo crítico en el campo de las artes visuales y la estética, integrando la práctica artística con el análisis teórico.
details: The 2026-1 calendar ran from enrolment on 21-23 January 2026 (classes from 9 February) to the end of the term on 17 July 2026. Admission is once a year. Its course catalogue is drawing- and project-based, and no dedicated ceramics course was found. Contact: artesvisualesyestetica.fai@correounivalle.edu.co, +57 (2) 321-2309. Industrial Design is run by the Departamento de Diseño (Edificio E11; fai.direccion.disenoindustrial@correounivalle.edu.co).

name: Pontificia Universidad Javeriana Cali – Artes Visuales
description: An eight-semester, project-based Visual Arts degree in the Faculty of Creation and Habitat. It includes a sculpture project on space and context, two printmaking courses and painting studios, and students share projects with architecture and design students.
descriptionOriginal: El arte no adorna: el arte propone, cuestiona y construye futuro.
details: Maestro(a) en Artes Visuales: SNIES 53475, 136 credits, in person, daytime. 2026 costs are COP 167.000 to apply and COP 11.419.000 per semester. The curriculum includes 'Proyecto 2 Escultura: Espacio y Contexto', Grabado I and II, Pintura, Fotografía and Museografía, plus electives. An open day (Expofamilia) is set for Saturday 7 November 2026. The department's course list also includes Taller de Escultura and Taller de Tridimensionalidad.

name: Institución Universitaria de las Culturas y las Artes Populares (IUIPC) – Licenciatura en Artes Plásticas y Visuales Populares
nameEnglish: IUIPC – Degree in Popular Plastic and Visual Arts
description: A new university degree from Cali's historic Instituto Popular de Cultura that trains artist-teachers in popular plastic and visual arts. It is taught through workshop practice and links traditional, emerging and popular art forms with community work.
descriptionOriginal: Un pregrado universitario único en el país, orientado al reconocimiento, la creación y la enseñanza de las artes plásticas y visuales populares.
details: The degree is SNIES 118367 (Registro Calificado, Resolución 000537 of 14 January 2026): 151 credits over 8 semesters. Admission is by a one-day test that includes drawing, easel painting and a modelling (three-dimensional) exercise, and the 30 highest scorers are selected. For 2026, online registration ran from 24 March to 20 May 2026. Check iuipc.edu.co for the next intake. Which campus teaches the degree was not confirmed; the address given is the main Coltabaco campus.

name: IUIPC – Escuela de Artes Plásticas y Fotografía Artística (programas ETDH)
nameEnglish: IUIPC School of Plastic Arts (vocational programmes)
address: Sede Coltabaco, Calle 12 # 1-12, Cali (other campuses: El Lido, Calle 2a No. 47-150; Porvenir, Calle 28 No. 5-74)
description: The Instituto Popular de Cultura's affordable vocational art school, for anyone who has finished ninth grade, trains plastic artists, sculptors, muralists and artisans. Its 'Gráfica Popular' group works in screen printing and ecological printmaking.
descriptionOriginal: Formación integral en Artes Plásticas y Fotografía Artística, basada en las tradiciones universales del arte y en las particularidades del entorno latinoamericano y colombiano.
details: These are Educación para el Trabajo y Desarrollo Humano programmes (37 credits; licences renewed 13 March 2025). The minimum age is 16 and applicants need a ninth-grade certificate. 2026 fees are COP 71.650 to register and COP 411.850 tuition for new students. For 2026-B, registration ran from 11 May to 16 June 2026, with admission tests from 30 June to 10 July. Classes run Monday to Saturday, 2-6 pm or 6-10 pm. Older city sources (2010) listed a 'Técnico laboral en cerámica artística' and a jewellery programme, but neither appears in the current offer; ask the school (escuela.artesplasticasyvisuales@iuipc.edu.co).

name: Universidad Autónoma de Occidente – Diseño Industrial
description: A nine-semester industrial design degree focused on product creation and responsible use of materials. It includes physical model-making, two courses on processes and materials, and digital fabrication.
descriptionOriginal: Carrera orientada a la creación de productos que respondan a las necesidades de los usuarios haciendo uso responsable y sostenible de los materiales.
details: The degree is SNIES 103338 (registro calificado Resolución 21346 of 14 November 2023, valid for 7 years), with 158 credits. Courses include Desarrollo de modelos físicos, Procesos y materiales I-II, Diseño y fabricación digital, and Arte y tecnología. The university also runs UAO Labs complementary workshops.

name: Fundación Academia de Dibujo Profesional (FADP)
description: A Cali design school offering short professional-technician programmes in fashion design, industrial-design production, interior design, architectural drawing and decoration, and graphic design.
descriptionOriginal: Técnico Profesional en Producción en Diseño Industrial; Diseño de Modas; Producción en Diseño de Interiores; Dibujo Arquitectónico y Decoración.
details: Several programmes are accredited (for example Diseño de Modas, SNIES 52513, and Diseño de Interiores, SNIES 103500). The industrial-design production programme lasts 6 semesters, in person, and covers model-making and prototyping for furniture, leather goods, footwear and other sectors. The Dibujo Arquitectónico y Decoración programme was renewed by MEN resolution 001243 of 21 January 2026. No ceramics programme is offered. The campus address was not on the pages checked.

name: Universidad de San Buenaventura Cali – Diseño de Vestuario
nameEnglish: San Buenaventura University Cali – Fashion and Costume Design
description: A clothing and fashion design degree in the Faculty of Architecture, Art and Design, with its own machine workshop (Taller de Máquinas) and a student magazine that has won awards.
descriptionOriginal: Nuestra facultad reafirma su identidad a partir de la enseñanza de la Arquitectura, del vestuario y de la gastronomía.
details: The faculty also offers Architecture, Culinary Sciences and a specialisation in Interior Design. Recent news includes nominations at the Premios Lápiz de Acero 2025 and 2026, and the programme magazine Pointer won the Premio Pixel Media 2025. Admission details and costs were not checked (a 2026 programme brochure is on the site).

name: La Linterna (taller de artes gráficas)
description: A typographic print shop founded in 1934 that still prints Cali's street posters by hand with movable type and linocut on presses dating back to the 1870s. It designed official Feria de Cali posters and, in 2025, its first film poster.
descriptionOriginal: Fundada en 1934, "patrimonio vivo de Cali"; más que un taller de impresión, un ícono de la gráfica popular latinoamericana.
details: Address from a Cali city bulletin (Dec 2024) on the 67th Feria de Cali poster, printed in linocut on 1870 machines. Its own site (lalinternacali.com) runs a shop of printed posters in the historic centre and shows the 68th Feria de Cali (2025) poster; WhatsApp +57 313 780 9394. In March 2025 its members led a two-day linocut and hand-press workshop at Poster House (New York). A 2019 city bulletin described a Taller Escuela de Artes Gráficas La Linterna created with the Fundación Escuela Taller de Cali; whether public classes run in Cali in 2026 could not be verified, so ask about visits or workshops.

name: Tropical Press
description: A small letterpress workshop in Cali's historic centre, facing the Plazoleta de San Francisco, run by designer José David García. Writers, designers and curious visitors set movable type there to print their own postcards, posters and poetry.
descriptionOriginal: Espacio de formación tipográfica y editorial donde escritores, diseñadores y curiosos crean postales, afiches y poesía impresa con tipos móviles.
details: El País Cali (July 2025) profiles the workshop and shows exercises from its sessions; it keeps Italian and American typefaces no longer produced. No street number, schedule, prices or booking channel were given. The photo captions name the founder 'José David González' while the text says García.

name: Laboratorio de Innovación y Diseño - Valle del Cauca (Artesanías de Colombia)
nameEnglish: Artesanías de Colombia Innovation and Design Lab, Valle del Cauca
description: The Valle del Cauca branch of the national craft agency's design labs, giving artisans advice on product design, production quality, marketing and brand registration. Weaving is the department's largest craft, followed by bead jewellery and carpentry; in Cali the lab works with ceramic and weaving artisans on a contemporary line and with artisans of Parque Loma de la Cruz.
descriptionOriginal: El Laboratorio presta asesorías en desarrollo humano y socio organizativo; diseño, producción y calidad de desarrollo de productos; acompañamiento comercial.
details: Crafts listed for the metro area: banana-stem fibre (calceta de plátano) in Cali; contemporary craft, cabinetmaking, leatherwork and jewellery in Palmira and Yumbo. The page cites Nasa women weavers of Altos Nápoles (Cali) making jigras. Contact is by the lab's email (obfuscated on the page) or Artesanías de Colombia's WhatsApp +57 305 772 7539; no local street address is given. Municipalities are prioritised through an annual call. Artesanías de Colombia also ran the Pacífico Artesanal fair in Cali on 26-29 Dec 2025 (separate news page).

name: Litoral: Artesanías del Pacífico (Secretaría de Cultura de Cali)
description: A city programme that pairs master artisans with paid apprentices to pass on Pacific and southwestern Colombian crafts: basketry, weaving, ceramics, embroidery, jewellery, wood, leather, metal, mosaic and lutherie. It also helps artisans sell their work at fairs in Cali and elsewhere.
descriptionOriginal: Litoral conecta a quienes conservan estos conocimientos con nuevas personas interesadas en aprenderlos.
details: It runs two cycles a year. Cycle 2026-I had 30 masters and 150 apprentices. For 2026-II, the call for masters (adults living in Cali who carry Pacific or southwestern craft knowledge) closed 25 June 2026 with 83 participants. The apprentice call drew 488 applications, and 150 apprentices were selected on 18 Aug 2026. Apprentices receive a stipend conditional on attendance and programme commitments. Applications go through the Secretaría de Cultura's yearly calls (Banco de Artesanos del programa Litoral), so watch for the 2027-I call. Workshop locations were not given. Registration has been via www.culturaenlineacali.com and requires joining the Banco de Artesanos de Cali (2026-I call, 30 Jan-13 Feb 2026).

name: Cali Entretejida
description: A citizen crochet movement of more than 500 weavers who make 'ringlete' granny pieces, inspired by San Antonio's traditional flowerpots, and join them into woven 'skies' over city streets: 80 metres over Calle de la Escopeta in 2025 and a 79.7-metre canopy on the Bulevar de Oriente for Cali's 490th anniversary in 2026.
descriptionOriginal: "Seguimos sembrando esperanza, unión, respeto y amor por nuestra ciudad" (Amparo Jiménez, Sociedad de Mejoras Públicas).
details: Led by Fundación Fanalca and the Sociedad de Mejoras Públicas de Cali with the Comunidad de Tejido. The 2026 collective weaving day was 25 July 2026 at the Bulevar de Oriente, with sign-up through a Google Form linked in the city bulletin; open to all ages and to anyone who weaves. A related World Wide Knit in Public Day gathering was held at Jardín Plaza in June 2025. No fixed weekly meetup or contact person was published; check the organisers' channels for the next installation.

name: José Miguel García Villa (joyería en filigrana)
nameEnglish: José Miguel García Villa, filigree jeweller
description: A filigree jeweller from Guapi on the Cauca coast, now based in Cali, where he teaches the fine-wire technique to women. He has been a master in the city's Litoral programme since 2024 and represented Cali at Territorios Vivos in Paris in 2026.
descriptionOriginal: La joyería en filigrana, a cargo de José Miguel García Villa, quien enseña este oficio a mujeres.
details: No workshop name, address or class schedule was published; the most practical route to learning with him is the Litoral programme (Secretaría de Cultura de Cali). El Tiempo (15 July 2026) confirms his participation in Litoral in 2024, 2025 and the first half of 2026.

name: AneleH - Telar Creativo (Bertha Helena Mosquera)
nameEnglish: AneleH Creative Loom, Bertha Helena Mosquera
description: The weaving brand of Cali artisan Bertha Helena Mosquera, who has devoted her career to horizontal (floor) loom weaving and combines traditional technique with contemporary design. She was one of four Litoral artisans chosen to represent Cali in Paris in 2026.
descriptionOriginal: Ha dedicado su trayectoria a la tejeduría en telar horizontal y, desde su marca AneleH-Telar Creativo, combina tradición y creación contemporánea.
details: The bulletin says she comes from Cali's rural area. No studio address, class offer or online shop was found, and whether she teaches publicly was not stated.

name: Carmencita Cárdenas Chiripua (cestería en werregue)
nameEnglish: Carmencita Cárdenas Chiripua, Wounaan werregue weaver
description: A Wounaan artisan who weaves werregue, the finely coiled palm-fibre basketry of the Pacific, and passes the craft on from the hillside neighbourhood of Siloé in Cali.
descriptionOriginal: Carmencita Cárdenas Chiripua, quien trabaja el werregue y transmite este saber desde Siloé.
details: Part of the Litoral programme and of the 2026 Paris delegation. No workshop name, address or class details were published; contact via the Secretaría de Cultura's Litoral programme.

name: Artesanía Magüí (Deira Tomasa Quiñones)
description: The basketry workshop of Deira Tomasa Quiñones, a weaver from Magüí Payán (Nariño) who learned paja tetera and rampira basketry as a child and in Cali weaves baskets from salvaged steel strapping with a team of women. She is a Litoral artisan and travelled to Paris with the programme in 2026.
descriptionOriginal: Cestería en paja tetera; conecta con el tejido desde su herencia familiar.
details: Her Colombia Artesanal profile (colombiaartesanal.com.co) gives the workshop address Carrera 49H # 56I-81 near Ciudad Verde, a shop on level 4 of Parque Artesanal Loma de la Cruz, phone 321 706 7448, artesaniamagui@gmail.com and Instagram @tomasa_artesania, with a 'schedule your visit' option. It notes that traditional fibres are hard to get in Cali, so she mostly weaves zuncho (steel strapping). No class schedule or fees were published.

name: Tradición Entretejida (Rosa Imelda Cabeza Quiera)
description: The basketry of Rosa Imelda Cabeza Quiera, a weaver from Guapi who has woven since the age of seven and makes 'cuatro tetas' baskets, bags and planters from natural fibres coloured with natural dyes.
descriptionOriginal: Artesana que teje tradición y biodiversidad en cada canasta, con fibras y tintes naturales.
details: Shown at the 29 Grados creative space in the Coltabaco building during Cali's Semana de la Biodiversidad (September 2025). The bulletin gives no workshop address, contact or teaching offer.

name: MAO - Manos a la Obra
description: A Cali booking platform for small, beginner-friendly craft workshops held in cafés and partner spaces in El Peñón, San Antonio and elsewhere. Its weekly agenda leans on fibre: crochet, macramé, botanical embroidery, amigurumi and pet-portrait embroidery, alongside watercolour and kintsugi.
descriptionOriginal: Talleres y experiencias creativas en Cali.
details: Listings for late October to December 2026 include Crochet at Café Macondo (COP 40,000), Macramé (COP 40,000), Bordado botánico (COP 38,000), Mini Amigurumi (COP 38,000) and Borda tu mascota (COP 55,000), at venues such as Somos Legados, Dulcinea Café vintage and Indeleble Café (El Peñón) and Facundo (San Antonio). Each event page gives the exact address and booking; contact by WhatsApp +57 302 692 3244. Instructors are not named on the listings.

name: Piolas y Piolas
nameEnglish: Piolas y Piolas yarn and cord shop
description: A Cali fibre-supply shop, physical and online: cotton and eco-cotton macramé cords, yarns from brands such as Cisne, DMC, Nako and Silvia, embroidery threads, ribbons, crochet, knitting and macramé tools, dyes and amigurumi kits.
descriptionOriginal: Insumos para tejidos y manualidades: piolas, hilazas, lanas, hilos, cintas y accesorios.
details: Store hours Mon-Fri 8am-6pm, Sat 8am-5pm; tel. +57 315 519 4758, admin@piolasypiolas.com. Example price: 2-3 mm eco-cotton macramé cord at COP 9,500. Free shipping to main cities on orders over COP 300,000.

name: Escuela Johanna Ortiz (Escuela J.O.)
description: The couture training school of Cali fashion designer Johanna Ortiz. Six-month intensive cohorts of about 20 students, many with no prior experience, learn high-end garment construction until they can finish a piece for the brand; more than 1,150 people have trained, and graduates join the atelier or open their own workshops.
descriptionOriginal: "Muchas veces lo que falta no son las ganas, sino la oportunidad." (Johanna Ortiz)
details: FashionUnited reports that the company pays students a salary during training and that it mainly serves women and young people from vulnerable backgrounds. In 2025 Escuela J.O. also taught free complementary couture, pattern-making and design modules (40 h + 50 h) with SENA and Fundación Club Campestre at the Mi Cali Bella se Integra centre, Calle 2B 2Oe #90-27, Bajo Jordán, comuna 18 (Cali city bulletin, 15 Mar 2025). No public application page was found; ask the brand or Cali's TIO office about new cohorts.

name: Museo La Tertulia (Museo de Arte Moderno La Tertulia)
nameEnglish: La Tertulia Museum of Modern Art
description: Cali's modern art museum, which turned 70 in 2026. It holds a major collection of Latin American graphic art, including works from the historic Bienales Americanas de Artes Gráficas, and runs guided tours, workshops and community curating labs. It has also hosted the Salón BAT de Arte Popular, which shows self-taught makers from the Pacific region.
descriptionOriginal: Las exposiciones del Museo La Tertulia serán de entrada libre este domingo, 17 de mayo (El País, mayo 2026).
details: El País (15 May 2026) reported free entry to the exhibition halls on 17 May 2026, 2-6 p.m., with guided tours. In April-June 2025 it hosted the regional Pacific and Putumayo show of the VIII Salón BAT de Arte Popular (94 works by self-taught artists, some made from recycled materials). After the 10 August 2026 earthquake, El País (23 Aug 2026) listed La Tertulia among venues closed for technical evaluation, and The Art Newspaper (19 Aug) said it remained closed to the public. Its Cinemateca was screening again for the Festival Internacional de Cine de Cali on 24-25 Oct 2026, but whether the exhibition halls have reopened isn't confirmed. Check the museum's own channels before visiting.

name: Museo Arqueológico MUSA La Merced
description: An archaeological museum in the colonial convent of La Merced (founded 1541), the oldest religious building in Cali. It sits beside a religious art museum and is a good place to study pre-Hispanic pottery from southwestern Colombia up close.
descriptionOriginal: Más que una iglesia, es un complejo religioso conformado por el museo arqueológico y el museo de arte religioso (Alcaldía de Cali, marzo 2026).
details: El País (15 May 2026) listed MUSA, Carrera 4 #6-59, with free entry on Saturday 16 May 2026, 9 a.m.-6 p.m. Caution: after the 10 August 2026 earthquake, the Secretaría de Cultura rated the Convento La Merced 'amarillo (uso restringido)' (El País, 23 Aug 2026), and the church itself was damaged. The museum's current opening status was not confirmed. Regular hours and fees for 2026 were not found. Travel and city sources describe the collection as pre-Hispanic ceramics plus colonial religious art.

name: Museo del Oro Calima (Banco de la República)
description: The Banco de la República's archaeological museum in Cali. Its displays on the Calima region's pre-Hispanic cultures cover goldwork alongside ceramics and other materials, and it runs free guided visits of its collections.
descriptionOriginal: Visita guiada por las colecciones del museo que narran la historia precolombina de la región (Alcaldía de Cali, mayo 2025).
details: The Alcaldía de Cali announced a free guided visit on Saturday 17 May 2025 at 10 a.m. for Museum Day (Red de Museos MUVAC). The Banco de la República's own pages (banrepcultural.org, banrep.gov.co) could not be opened because of bot protection, so 2026 programming and the museum's status after the August 2026 earthquake were not verified. City and travel listings describe free entry Tuesday to Saturday, but those hours are not confirmed for 2026.

name: Museo Hernando Tejada
description: A small museum on the life and inspirations of Hernando 'Tejadita' Tejada, the Cali artist known for his carved and painted wooden figures and the city's 'Gato del Río'. It opened in 2024 to mark the artist's centenary.
descriptionOriginal: El museo se centra principalmente en el estilo de vida del maestro Tejada, su diversidad y las fuentes de su inspiración (Alcaldía de Cali, mayo 2025).
details: Listed by the Alcaldía de Cali for Museum Day on 18 May 2025 (hours that day 12 m.-7 p.m.), inside Finestral Gallery Art. A 2024 city bulletin says it opened that year for the centenary and is about 150 m from El Gato del Río. Regular 2026 hours, fees and status after the August 2026 earthquake were not verified. Tejada's railway-station murals, a separate site, were damaged by the quake and are being restored (El País, Aug 2026).

name: Galería de Arte Humberto Hernández – Centro Cultural Colombo Americano de Cali
description: The art gallery of Cali's Centro Cultural Colombo Americano in the north of the city. It mounts rotating exhibitions (in 2023 it showed Omar Rayo's intaglio prints with the Museo Rayo) and offers guided visits and occasional hands-on workshops.
descriptionOriginal: Galería de Arte Humberto Hernández – Centro Cultural Colombo Americano de Cali. Visita guiada: 9:30 a.m. Taller de ilustración en acuarela: 10:00 a.m. (El País, mayo 2026).
details: For Museum Day on Saturday 16 May 2026, El País listed a guided visit (9:30 a.m.) and a free watercolour illustration workshop (10 a.m.). The 2026 exhibition calendar, workshop costs and status after the August 2026 earthquake were not verified. The Colombo Americano's own event page returned 404.

name: Museo Arqueológico Calima (INCIVA)
description: The Valle del Cauca's archaeological museum in Calima-El Darién, run by INCIVA, the department's heritage institute. It presents the pre-Hispanic cultures of the Calima region, whose ceramics and goldwork are among the best known in southwestern Colombia.
descriptionOriginal: Reabrieron al público el Museo Arqueológico Calima, en Calima-El Darién, tras las afectaciones ocasionadas por el sismo (Occidente, sept. 2026).
details: Closed after the 10 August 2026 earthquake. Diario Occidente (10 Sep 2026) reported it had reopened after safety checks, with only minor damage to collections and exhibits. El País (May 2026) listed it as open 9 a.m.-5 p.m. on Museum Day, 18 May 2026. Regular hours and fees were not confirmed. As of the same report, INCIVA's Museo de Ciencias Naturales in Cali and Hacienda El Paraíso were still temporarily closed for repairs.

name: Museo Rayo de Arte Moderno Latinoamericano
description: The museum Omar Rayo founded in his hometown of Roldanillo in 1981, in a distinctive building designed by Leopoldo Gout. It turned 45 in 2026 and keeps up a busy rotation of shows, recently including Spanish 20th-century prints (serigraphy, etching), aluminium sculpture by Jesús Tibaduiza and drawings by Julio Dacunha.
descriptionOriginal: El Museo Rayo abrirá tres nuevas exposiciones en sus salas, cuya inauguración será este sábado 17 de enero, a las 4:00 p. m. con entrada libre (El País, enero 2026).
details: El País (15 Jan 2026) announced three exhibitions opening 17 January 2026 for its 45th anniversary, curated by Miguel González. In Oct 2025 it was open Monday to Sunday, 9 a.m.-6 p.m. Roldanillo was badly hit by the 10 August 2026 earthquake. Diario Occidente (11 Aug 2026) reported the museum was not damaged, but an El Tiempo headline suggested otherwise. Confirm it is open before making the trip north of Cali.

name: Lugar a Dudas
nameEnglish: Lugar a Dudas (independent contemporary art space)
description: An independent contemporary art organisation working in Cali since 2005. It keeps a specialist art library and documentation centre (CEDOC) and runs exhibitions, a curatorial micro-school, talks, workshops such as portfolio and artist-statement sessions, artist clinics and study groups.
descriptionOriginal: La escuela ecosomática se desarrollará durante 2026 en cuatro módulos, cada uno guiado por un invitado nacional o internacional.
details: In 2026 its 'El Gimnasio' programme runs the Escuela Ecosomática: four modules (Arturo Escobar, Marie Bardet, The Sensing Salon, Fred Moten), each with an in-person intensive and a four-session study group. Module pages were published June-July 2026. Costs, enrolment and dates are not given on the site. The residency programme ran until the pandemic and does not appear to be active now. The address was not stated on the pages opened. The city has co-funded a training grant with the foundation (Beca de Formación en la Estancia Pedagógica en Escuela Incierta) in past years.

name: Parque Artesanal Loma de la Cruz
nameEnglish: Loma de la Cruz Craft Park
description: Cali's permanent open-air craft park, opened in 1990 on a hillside with plazas and a small theatre. Resident artisans sell their work there, and the Secretaría de Cultura runs fairs, awards and community workshops taught by the park's artisans.
descriptionOriginal: Convocatoria para la realización de talleres de artes visuales con enfoque en artesanías, dirigida exclusivamente a los artesanos del Parque Artesanal Loma de la Cruz.
details: For its 35th anniversary in 2025 the city held craft fairs with live music on several Saturdays (31 May to 13 Sep 2025). In Oct 2025 the Secretaría de Cultura funded ten free craft workshops of at least 20 hours (minimum 10 participants each), taught by park artisans, 29 Oct-7 Nov 2025. A Nov 2025 call (Premiación al oficio artesanal) awarded nine park artisans. Contact: lomadelacruz@cali.gov.co. No 2026 schedule was found, and the park's status after the August 2026 earthquake was not checked.

name: Pacífico Artesanal (Artesanías de Colombia)
description: A craft fair run by Artesanías de Colombia during the Feria de Cali. It brings around 60 craft workshops from the four Pacific departments (Cauca, Chocó, Nariño and Valle del Cauca), with live craft demonstrations, music and sales.
descriptionOriginal: Pacífico Artesanal 2025 contará con la participación de 60 talleres artesanales, provenientes de los cuatro departamentos de la región Pacífico.
details: The third edition ran 26-29 December 2025, 10 a.m.-9 p.m., on the Bulevar del Río during the Feria de Cali. An earlier edition (Dec 2024) was held at the Parque de las Banderas with about 80 artisans. The Feria de Cali 2026 is scheduled for 25-30 December 2026, but a 2026 Pacífico Artesanal had not been announced in the sources found.

name: Festival Petronio Álvarez – componente de artesanías
description: Cali's huge festival of Pacific music has a craft component in which dozens of makers sell natural-fibre weaving, filigree jewellery, wood carving and basketry alongside traditional food, drink and fashion.
descriptionOriginal: Tejidos en fibras naturales, joyería en filigrana, tallas en madera... cestería (Alcaldía de Cali, agosto 2025).
details: The 2025 edition drew more than 800,000 people. The 30th edition, planned for 10-17 Aug 2026, was suspended after the 10 August 2026 earthquake. About 120 tradition bearers instead took part as guests of honour at Bogotá's Feria del Hogar (Corferias, 3-20 Sep 2026). On 27 Aug 2026 the Secretaría de Cultura said the festival would still be held in Cali in the second half of 2026, date to be announced (El País). Meanwhile, smaller gatherings filled the gap, such as the Juntanza Pacífica at the Casa de Herencia Guapireña in San Antonio (30 Aug 2026, with a free turban workshop). No rescheduled date had been confirmed at the time of this check.

name: Festival de Macetas
description: An annual festival of the 'macetas', a Cali sugar craft now recognised as national intangible heritage. Women artisans shape alfeñique sugar paste into figures mounted on maguey stems, which godparents give to their godchildren. Stalls go up across the city, alongside talks, live kitchen workshops and family activities.
descriptionOriginal: 98 portadoras de este saber patrimonial... estarán ofreciendo sus macetas en diferentes espacios emblemáticos de la ciudad.
details: The 26th edition ran 24-29 June 2026, organised by the association of sugar artisans with the Secretaría de Cultura. It had 98 artisans with stalls at Parque San Antonio, Parque de las Banderas, Bulevar del Río, Bulevar del Oriente and shopping centres, plus a first international meeting on traditional sweets (25-26 June, Centro Cultural de Cali). It is held every year around the Día del Ahijado (29 June).

name: Mercadillo Torre de la Vega (Casa Obeso Mejía)
nameEnglish: Torre de la Vega market at Casa Obeso Mejía
description: A weekend market of local makers and small brands at the historic Casa Obeso Mejía in the west of Cali. Some stalls sell craft goods, others food, with free entry and a family- and pet-friendly setting.
descriptionOriginal: De este tradicional mercadillo participan diversos comercios. Algunos comercializan productos artesanales, otros alimentos.
details: It restarted after the earthquake with a Pacific-themed edition on 29-30 Aug 2026, 10 a.m.-6 p.m., which also served as a donation drop-off point. Dates are announced on Casa Obeso Mejía's social media. The source does not say how often it runs or how to apply as a vendor.

name: Feria Entre Manos (Litoral: Artesanías del Pacífico)
description: A city-run sales fair for artisans of the Litoral programme, set up to help makers recover income after the 2026 earthquake. It shows basketry, jewellery, chaquira beadwork, woodwork, ceramics and weaving from the Pacific and southwestern Colombia, both in person and online.
descriptionOriginal: Oficios como cestería, joyería, tejeduría en chaquira, trabajo en madera, cerámica y tejeduría.
details: The in-person edition ran 16-20 Sep 2026, 10 a.m.-7 p.m., on the second-floor connecting bridge of Pacific Center, with a parallel virtual sale on Litoral's digital platform. The source does not say whether it will recur.

name: Portafolio de convocatorias Cali Distrito Cultural 2026
description: Cali's yearly package of public arts funding calls from the Secretaría de Cultura. It includes Estímulos (creation and research grants), Circulación, Concertación for non-profit organisations, Formación, the Litoral artisans' bank and city festivals.
descriptionOriginal: El portafolio 2026 está diseñado con las convocatorias de Circulación, Estímulos, Concertación, Formación, Banco de Artesanos del programa Litoral y Eventos de ciudad.
details: The 2026 portfolio was announced on 30 Jan 2026 with COP 13,000 million. A second-half round (Concertación: Interculturalidad and Reconocimiento, COP 935 million for 43 non-profit projects) opened on 12 June 2026 and closed 5-9 July 2026, through www.culturaenlineacali.com. Eligibility differs by line (many require a Cali-based person or organisation), so read each call's terms. After the August 2026 earthquake the Secretaría also opened a channel for affected cultural workers to report damage.

name: Taller Gilberto y Óscar Granja (Barniz de Pasto)
description: Family workshop of master Gilberto Granja and his son Óscar, keepers of the barniz de Pasto technique, in which mopa-mopa resin is chewed, stretched into thin colored sheets and laid onto turned and carved wooden pieces. Óscar Granja also opens the workshop to visitors, letting them handle the raw resin, try the stretching process and make a small piece to take home.
descriptionOriginal: Barniz de Pasto. Recommended by Artesanías de Colombia; listed as a Homo Faber 2026 artisan.
details: Homo Faber lists visiting hours as Monday to Friday 08:00-12:00 / 14:00-17:00 and Saturday 09:00-13:00 (Spanish only). Artesanías de Colombia's Colombia Artesanal platform (colombiaartesanal.com.co/taller/oscar-granja/) describes a bookable half-day hands-on workshop for 2-5 people, schedule agreed with the visitor, arranged directly with Óscar Granja. The street address on Homo Faber is written oddly ("3050 Calle 19a"), so confirm the exact location when booking. Barniz de Pasto mopa-mopa is on UNESCO's urgent-safeguarding list; a Diario del Sur piece dated 2026-10-14 also mentions barniz de Pasto workshop exhibitions in Nariño's October 2026 cultural agenda. Price not published.

name: Museo del Carnaval de Negros y Blancos
description: Year-round home of Pasto's carnival art, showing monumental papier-mâché and recycled-material sculptures from the January Desfile Magno floats, plus masks, costumes and props made by comparsas and murgas. A rare chance to study large-scale sculptural making techniques up close outside carnival season.
descriptionOriginal: Espacio permanente dedicado a inmortalizar y exhibir la riqueza cultural y artística de esta celebración.
details: Located in the Centro Cultural Pandiaco, which houses Pasto's municipal Secretaría de Cultura. Opening hours and admission were not given in the source; check with the Alcaldía de Pasto / Secretaría de Cultura before visiting.

name: Carnaval de Negros y Blancos de Pasto
description: UNESCO-listed carnival whose January parades are a showcase of handmade making: giant papier-mâché floats (carrozas), costumes and masks built by local artists roll through the city on 6 January in the Desfile Magno. The organizers count some 13,000 artists taking part.
descriptionOriginal: El Desfile Magno, un día apoteósico donde la creatividad se siente por toda la senda; disfraces, comparsas y carrozas emergen e inundan la ciudad.
details: The official site lists the core days: 2 January (Carnavalito), 3 January (colectivos coreográficos), 4 January (llegada de la Familia Castañeda), 5 January (Juego de identidad / painted faces) and 6 January (Desfile Magno with carrozas), plus a pre-carnival agenda. Organized by Corpocarnaval. Dates for the January 2027 edition were not checked.

name: Programa de Artes Plásticas, Facultad de Artes, Universidad del Cauca
nameEnglish: University of Cauca Visual Arts programme
address: Facultad de Artes, Casa Torres, Carrera 6 No. 3-14, Sector Histórico, Popayán
description: Public university degree in plastic arts run from the Casa Torres in Popayán's historic centre, with two- and three-dimensional studio work; the curriculum includes a ceramics course and optional workshops in digital and analog printing. Entry is through an in-person practical aptitude test.
descriptionOriginal: La prueba de aptitud tiene como objetivo evaluar las habilidades expresivas y creativas del aspirante a través de un ejercicio práctico, bidimensional y/o tridimensional.
details: The aptitude-test guide for the first academic period of 2026 set the in-person test for 5 December 2025 at the Facultad de Artes - Casa Torres (morning 7:30-12:00, afternoon 1:30-6:00). Admissions contact on the guide: admisiones@unicauca.edu.co. This is a formal degree programme; no open community courses were found.

name: Popayán Fashion Week
description: Annual design showcase organized by the Cámara de Comercio del Cauca in Popayán's main square, where regional designers bring artisan techniques onto the runway. The 2026 edition centred on memory, territory and craft, including collections made with Cauca women's associations and with Nariño weavers and embroiderers.
descriptionOriginal: Reúne diseñadores y marcas con propuestas de moda, identidad, sostenibilidad y saberes artesanales en el Cauca.
details: The 2026 (eleventh) edition ran 24-26 September 2026 in Parque Caldas after being rescheduled following the 10 August earthquake. Featured projects included Tinta Roja's work with the women's association Las Manualitas and XZAE, a Nariño brand working with weaving, embroidery, crochet and macramé artisans. The next edition's dates are not yet published. Fashion-led rather than a hands-on workshop.

name: Cestería en rollo de Guacamayas
description: Small northern Boyacá town near El Cocuy whose families weave brightly coloured fique and straw into baskets, fruit bowls, mats, bags and figures with a distinctive braiding and decoration technique. Visitors can tour the places where the pieces are made and sold.
descriptionOriginal: Los pobladores confeccionan bolsos, canastos, muñecos, carpetas, fruteros y toda una amplia gama de tejidos en fique y paja.
details: Ley 2614 de 2026 (28 July 2026) names 'las cestas tejidas en fique de Guacamayas' among the Boyacá craft practices on the departmental artisans' route. No specific workshop, opening hours or class offer was verified; plan a visit through the municipality or Boyacá tourism (Situr). The craft is widely described as holding a Denominación de Origen (seen in search results, not on an opened page).

name: Artesanos de Nobsa: ruanas y tejidos en lana
nameEnglish: Nobsa wool ruana weavers and artisans
description: Boyacá town known for hand-loomed sheep's-wool ruanas and blankets, with family workshops around the plaza; its artisans also work forged iron, bells, furniture, leather and stone. The municipality actively promotes its makers, including a 2026 sales showcase that took Nobsa crafts to Medellín.
descriptionOriginal: Productos elaborados con manos expertas, entre ellos forja, muebles, lana, tejidos, campanas, marroquinería, artesanías en piedra.
details: '¡Nobsa quiere a Medellín!' ran 24 July-10 August 2026 at Centro Comercial Unicentro Medellín, organized by the Alcaldía de Nobsa. Ley 2614 de 2026 lists 'las ruanas y tejeduras en lana de Nobsa' on the Boyacá artisans' route. The town also hosts a ruana festival each year (dates have varied; regional press reported 10-12 July for 2026, not opened). No individual workshop or class schedule was verified.

name: Cestería en chin de Tenza y Sutatenza
description: Basket-weaving tradition of the Valle de Tenza, where artisans in Tenza and neighbouring Sutatenza weave baskets from chin (caña de Castilla), split giant cane. It is one of the craft practices the 2026 national law singles out for safeguarding and youth training in Boyacá.
descriptionOriginal: Las cestas tejidas en Chin o caña de Castilla de Tenza y Sutatenza.
details: Named in article 2(g) of Ley 2614 de 2026, which tasks the Ministerio de las Culturas, SENA and the Gobernación de Boyacá with training programmes for young people in these techniques. No specific workshop, cooperative or opening hours were verified; treat this as a craft-town lead and contact the municipalities.

name: Tour del fique en Ecofibras
address: Half a block from the main park, Curití
description: Hands-on fique experience in Curití, the town known for its fique weaving: visitors learn the fibre's history, see how it is washed, dried and dyed, then watch the artisans' weaving techniques and try weaving themselves under their guidance. Run by curiteña fiquera Deisy Liliana Mejía Sierra, manager of Ecofibras.
descriptionOriginal: Una experiencia para conocer cada etapa de la transformación y para tejer bajo la guía de los fiqueros de Curití.
details: Vanguardia (October 2025) reports the tour lasts 30 minutes to an hour and costs between COP 4,000 and 8,000. No booking channel or opening hours were given; ask locally near the main park. Curití also has a collective trademark 'Fique de Curití'.

name: Taller de papel artesanal de la Fundación San Lorenzo de Barichara
nameEnglish: San Lorenzo Foundation handmade paper workshop
description: Long-running handmade-paper workshop a few blocks from Barichara's plaza, where local plant fibres such as fique and pineapple are turned into sheets of paper and tinted with turmeric and achiote. Groups can join hands-on sessions that walk through each stage of the process.
descriptionOriginal: Taller de papel artesanal en la Fundación San Lorenzo de Barichara, donde transformamos fibras naturales en arte.
details: The September 2025 Festiver film festival ran a creative papermaking session here, producing fique and pineapple paper with turmeric and achiote colours. The foundation was formalized in 2001 after a workshop led by Mexican paper artist Juan Manuel de la Rosa. Opening hours, prices and how individuals book were not verified.

name: Taller de técnicas artesanales: Tejiendo con Barichara (Universidad del Rosario y Fundación Montechico)
nameEnglish: Weaving with Barichara: craft techniques course
description: Intensive summer course taught in Barichara with the Fundación Montechico, where three workshop leaders from art, agriculture, architecture and craft teach earth building, papermaking, weaving and dyeing with local materials like soil, fique, pineapple, indigo, achiote and amanda. Participants follow each material from source to finished piece and develop their own projects.
descriptionOriginal: Los participantes aprenderán técnicas de construcción, manufactura de papel, tejeduría y tintorería, observando el proceso desde su origen hasta su aplicación.
details: 2026 edition: 23 June-3 July 2026, hybrid format, 44 hours (23-25 June 5-7 pm online/introductory; 29 June-3 July 8 am-8 pm in Barichara). Registration was closed at the time of checking. The 2025 edition (16-21 June 2025) cost COP 2,940,000 including 5 nights' lodging and meals; 2026 pricing not checked. Fundación Montechico runs its own programmes in earth building, fibre papermaking and natural dyes; watch for a 2027 edition.

name: Salón Barichara ViveArte
address: Capilla de Jesús, cementerio municipal, Barichara
description: Annual salon showing work by artists born in or based in Barichara, held in the cemetery's Capilla de Jesús. The third edition in 2025 gathered 28 local artists and paid tribute to sculptor Alejandro Quintero, a reference for the town's stone-carving tradition.
descriptionOriginal: Una muestra que reúne a 28 artistas del municipio y rinde homenaje al escultor Alejandro Quintero, referente de la talla en piedra.
details: 2025 (third) edition ran until 13 October 2025. A 2026 edition was not confirmed. Free/paid entry not stated.

name: Festival Internacional de la Imagen
description: Long-running festival of art, design, science, technology and research-creation linked to the Universidad de Caldas and Universidad Jorge Tadeo Lozano communities, with an international seminar, academic forum, exhibitions, sound pieces, digital cinema, workshops and conversations.
descriptionOriginal: El Festival Internacional de la Imagen celebra en 2026 su versión 25, como espacio de encuentro entre arte, diseño, ciencia, tecnología e investigación-creación.
details: 2026 (25th) edition: Bogotá 10-13 September, Manizales 14-18 September 2026, with Chile as guest country. Passes are priced by category (for example, U. Caldas and U. Tadeo undergraduates free; other rates listed on the site). Leans toward media and digital art rather than traditional craft.

name: Exposición Artesanal de Armenia
description: Annual craft fair in Armenia's convention centre bringing together around 160 artisans from across Colombia and invited countries, with traditional and contemporary handmade pieces for sale.
descriptionOriginal: Un evento que reúne la creatividad, la cultura y el talento detrás del arte hecho a mano.
details: The 11th edition (2025) ran 26 April-4 May 2025 with 160 national artisans and 20 guest countries (Afghanistan as guest of honour), free entry on some days and doors from 10:00 a.m. Crónica del Quindío ran a headline on 9 May 2026 reporting more than 160 exhibitors at the 2026 edition (headline seen on a tag listing; article not opened). Expect a late-April/May edition in 2027.

name: Cestería en bejuco de Filandia
description: Coffee-region town famous for baskets woven from bejuco (forest vines), originally made for coffee pickers; craft workshops show visitors how the canastos are made, and a basketry interpretation centre presents the tradition.
descriptionOriginal: Talleres de artesanías: descubre el proceso de elaboración de los famosos canastos de bejuco y otras artesanías locales.
details: Travel and heritage sources mention the Centro de Interpretación de la Cestería de Bejucos and basket-maker families concentrated in the San José neighbourhood, plus the Fiestas del Canasto (reported variously for June or August). A 2025 academic article (Revista Hallazgos, Universidad Santo Tomás) studies the town's basketry artisans as a five-generation tradition. No dated 2026 workshop or opening hours were verified; evidence for current activity is from 2025 travel coverage.

name: Escuela de Artes y Oficios Santo Domingo
nameEnglish: Santo Domingo School of Arts and Crafts
description: Craft school founded in 1996 in restored colonial buildings in Bogotá's historic centre, teaching traditional trades to professional standard: floor, vertical and treadle loom weaving, textile dyeing with natural and synthetic dyes, embroidery, needle knitting, wood, leather, metalwork and leather bookbinding. Offers semester-long technical certificates, short weekend or weekday courses, and intensive workshops with visiting international masters.
descriptionOriginal: Formamos artesanos en oficios tradicionales desde 1996, ofrecemos programas técnico laboral, cursos libres y talleres intensivos con maestros internacionales.
details: Technical certificates are approved by the Secretaría de Educación de Bogotá. Vertical-loom programme: enrolment deadline 15 December 2026, classes start 18 January 2027, COP 2,011,000 per cycle, Monday-Friday 7-11 a.m. Textile dyeing (tintura) programme: one 624-hour cycle, COP 3,145,000 before 15 December 2026, Monday-Friday 7-11 a.m. Short 'cursos libres' run year-round in 4-hour sessions. Guided public visits on Fridays at 2:30 p.m. (book ahead). Contact: inscripciones@eaosd.org, (+57) 601 744 17 93.

name: Maestros Internacionales 2026, Escuela de Artes y Oficios Santo Domingo
nameEnglish: Visiting international masters workshops (silversmithing, wood turning)
description: Intensive workshops taught by visiting international masters, covering techniques outside the school's regular curriculum. The 2026 programme pairs a green-wood turning course with an architecture-inspired silversmithing workshop led by British jeweller Vicky Ambery Smith.
descriptionOriginal: Arquitectura y Platería: técnica histórica, objeto contemporáneo. Maestra británica Vicky Ambery Smith.
details: Silversmithing workshop: 3-24 November 2026, 8:00 a.m.-12:00 m or 1:30-5:30 p.m., 60 hours, COP 2,700,000; prerequisite basic metalwork. Wood-turning workshop 'Punto de Giro' with Spanish master Aitor Martínez ran 27 July-25 August 2026 (80 hours, COP 2,780,000; sold out). Certificate of attendance; payment in instalments possible. Contact inscripciones@eaosd.org.

name: Encuentro de artistas populares Salón BAT: Bogotá, Boyacá y Cundinamarca
nameEnglish: BAT Salon of popular art (central region)
address: Sala de Exposiciones, Universidad de La Salle, sede Candelaria, Carrera 2 # 10-70, Bogotá
description: Free exhibition of 90 works by 44 popular artists from Bogotá, Boyacá and Cundinamarca, spanning painting, sculpture, weaving, embroidery, printmaking and assemblage that tell the landscapes, trades and memories of central Colombia. Organized by Fundación BAT Colombia with the Universidad de La Salle.
descriptionOriginal: Pinturas, esculturas, tejidos, bordados, grabados y ensamblajes hacen parte del recorrido.
details: Open until 27 November 2026; Monday-Friday 10:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m., Saturday 10:00 a.m.-1:00 p.m.; free entry. Another press article gave a different La Salle address (Carrera 5 No. 59A-44), so confirm the venue before going. Temporary exhibition; the Salón BAT tours other regions in other years.

name: Salas LabCo de BibloRed
description: Free co-creation and fabrication labs inside Bogotá's public library network, where children, young people and adults learn by making with 3D printers, 3D pens, laser cutting, circuits and microscopes in guided, collaborative sessions.
descriptionOriginal: Las salas LabCo de la Red de Bibliotecas Públicas de Bogotá (BibloRed) continúan promoviendo el aprendizaje, la experimentación y la creatividad.
details: Activities are free; some require advance registration because lab capacity is limited. In August 2025 the LabCo at the Biblioteca Pública Gabriel García Márquez - El Tunal ran a 'Ciudad maker' workshop recreating Bogotá monuments with digital tools. The network reportedly has six LabCo rooms; check BibloRed's programme for which library hosts each session, schedules and age ranges.

name: Convocatoria Territorial "Artesanías, Territorio y Paz Total" y Laboratorios de Innovación y Diseño (Artesanías de Colombia)
nameEnglish: Artesanías de Colombia territorial call and Innovation and Design Labs
description: Annual national call by Colombia's state craft agency giving artisans, workshops, groups and associations in all 32 departments free access to its accompaniment programmes, including the Laboratorios de Gestión Social, Innovación y Creatividad, plus dedicated lines for ethnic communities and for victims and vulnerable populations.
descriptionOriginal: Una puerta de entrada para que artesanos y artesanas, así como grupos, comunidades y asociaciones, de los 32 departamentos y las seis regiones del país se inscriban.
details: The 2026 call was free and ran online until 21 February 2026 (selected list due 27 February 2026); regional press reported a later extension to 1 March. Aimed at working artisans and artisan groups rather than hobbyists. A 2027 call has not been announced; watch artesaniasdecolombia.com.co early in the year.

name: Museo de Antioquia
description: Medellín's historic art museum in the city centre, which marked its 145th anniversary in 2026 with 'MDA al Centro', a programme of concerts, workshops, tours and hands-on creation experiences linking art, music and the city's stories.
descriptionOriginal: El Museo de Antioquia celebra sus 145 años con MDA al Centro, una programación cultural que abre las puertas al encuentro, la exploración y la creación.
details: MDA al Centro runs until 30 October 2026 as part of Temporada Cultural Medellín 2026; some activities need prior registration with limited places, others are open. Check the museum's channels for its regular workshop programme after the anniversary season.

name: Makerspaces del Sistema de Bibliotecas Públicas de Medellín
address: Parque Biblioteca Presbítero José Luis Arroyave (San Javier), Parque Biblioteca Fernando Botero (San Cristóbal) and Parque Biblioteca Doce de Octubre
description: Three free, open-access makerspaces in Medellín's library parks, equipped for 3D modelling and printing, laser cutting and engraving, CNC, electronics, programming and robotics, with technical guidance for anyone wanting to prototype a personal or community project.
descriptionOriginal: No se requiere inscripción previa, cualquier persona puede acercarse al makerspace más cercano.
details: Free; no prior registration needed. Programme includes a weekly 'Taller de Hacedores' (Saturdays 2:00 p.m.), specialized training cycles, short 'Formando Makers' workshops and one-to-one project advice. Weekly schedule: bibliolabs.bibliotecasmedellin.gov.co. Contacts: makerspace.sanjavier@bibliomed.gov.co, makerspace.sancristobal@bibliomed.gov.co, makerspace.docedeoctubre@bibliomed.gov.co.

name: Escuela Taller Cartagena de Indias (Etcar)
description: A free workshop-school, more than 30 years old, that trains young people from Cartagena in traditional building and craft trades. Apprentices learn by doing on the city's fortifications, which the school manages.
descriptionOriginal: Su misión es "la formación de jóvenes en oficios tradicionales para la salvaguarda del patrimonio" (directora Sandra Schmalbach).
details: The January 2025 call offered 220 free places for 18-28-year-olds from estratos 1 and 2 who have finished at least 9th grade. Programmes were masonry, welding, carpentry, electricity, painting, gardening, cooking and a new dressmaking (confecciones) course. Training is 20% classroom and 80% practice, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., with protective gear, lunch and snacks provided. Applicants register online or at the school, then sit tests and an interview. The 2026 intake was not verified.

name: Museo de Oficios (Fuerte de San Fernando, Bocachica)
description: A community museum in the old vaults of the San Fernando fort on Tierrabomba island. It presents the living trades of Bocachica, such as canoe building, artisanal fishing, traditional hair braiding and midwifery, and local knowledge-keepers act as guides.
descriptionOriginal: Un espacio comunitario que recoge los saberes tradicionales de Bocachica, donde "la comunidad participa como guía y transmisora de los saberes".
details: Opened in 2024 by the Escuela Taller Cartagena de Indias and ICANH with support from the Ministerio de las Culturas, and created with the Bocachica community. In April 2025 entry to the fort was free and it was open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Boats leave from the La Bodeguita pier in the historic centre (15-20 minutes, about COP 10,000 each way plus a COP 5,000 maritime tax, per April 2025 figures). Plan half a day to a full day. Weaving is not among the trades listed in the source.

name: Las Bóvedas
description: A row of colonial vaults, once dungeons, built into the city wall at the far north of the historic centre. They now house craft shops selling Wayuu mochilas, San Jacinto-style hammocks, caña flecha sombreros vueltiaos and handmade jewellery from across the Caribbean.
descriptionOriginal: Antiguos calabozos convertidos en vitrinas artesanales con mochilas wayuu, hamacas, sombreros vueltiaos y joyería hecha a mano.
details: Prices vary by piece and season, and rise around holidays. The same April 2026 guide also points to stalls at Plaza de Santo Domingo (fique bags, ceramics), Plaza Santa Teresa (mochilas, hats, jewellery) and Parque del Centenario near the Torre del Reloj. No opening hours are given.

name: Museo del Oro Zenú
description: The Banco de la República's free museum of the Zenú, who lived across much of the Colombian Caribbean before colonisation. It shows goldwork, ceramics, textiles and tools, and explains the Zenú's hydraulic system for working the floodplain soils.
descriptionOriginal: Recorre la cultura Zenú con piezas de orfebrería, cerámica, textiles y herramientas.
details: Next to the Museo Histórico (MUHCA) on Plaza de Bolívar. Free entry. In April 2025 it was open Tuesday to Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Sunday 10 a.m. to 3 p.m., closed Monday. The Banco de la República cultural site was behind a bot check and could not be opened, so current programming was not verified.

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Cartagena (MAM)
description: A modern art museum in a former port warehouse facing the church of San Pedro Claver. It holds more than 300 works, mostly Latin American, and runs educational programmes.
descriptionOriginal: "Justo frente a la iglesia de San Pedro Claver", con más de 300 obras y énfasis en el arte latinoamericano.
details: Open since the late 1970s; the collection began with a donation from the OAS. April 2025 hours were Tuesday to Friday 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. and weekends 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., closed Monday. Prices then: COP 20,000 for Colombian adults (COP 10,000 for students, children and seniors) and COP 25,000 for general adults. Details of the educational programmes were not given.

name: Festival de la Cultura Wayuu
description: Uribia's long-running festival of Wayuu culture, with craft exhibitions and sales alongside music, dance and other cultural events over several days. It is a chance to see the work of Wayuu weavers gathered in one place.
descriptionOriginal: El XXXI Festival de la Cultura Wayuu reúne "muestras artesanales" y expresiones artísticas del pueblo Wayuu en Uribia.
details: The 31st (XXXI) edition opened on 6 June 2026 and ran over that weekend. The Gobernación de La Guajira took part through its Dirección de Turismo and the Casa del Artesano, alongside the Alcaldía de Uribia. The source does not name the venue or the craft exhibitors. Dates change from year to year, so check before travelling.

name: Casa del Artesano de La Guajira
description: A Gobernación de La Guajira programme that promotes the department's artisans, chiefly Wayuu weavers, at fairs in Colombia and abroad. It also offers training, credit access and business guidance.
descriptionOriginal: Iniciativa "liderada por la Gobernación de La Guajira" que promueve el "comercio justo" entre artesanos y marcas.
details: In 2026 it showed Guajira crafts at Feria AMA in Barranquilla in May, with mochilas and pieces in palma magüiza, fique and carnelian (piedra cornalina). It also backed Wayuu weavers at Territorios Vivos París during Paris Fashion Week in late September and October 2026. The sources do not give a physical address or say whether it runs a shop; the city is set to Riohacha, the department capital, as an approximation.

name: Feria Artesanal y Cultural del Sombrero Fino Vueltiao
nameEnglish: Sombrero Vueltiao Craft and Culture Fair
address: Pasaje de Exposiciones Zenú, Tuchín, Córdoba
description: Tuchín's annual fair of the sombrero vueltiao, the hat braided by Zenú weavers from caña flecha fibre. Makers from several departments come to sell, and the fair includes an exhibition on how the fibre goes from plant to hat.
descriptionOriginal: La XXVII Feria reunió en el Pasaje de Exposiciones Zenú a artesanos de siete departamentos; "cada vez es más difícil conseguir la caña flecha".
details: The 27th edition ran 9-11 January 2026 with 82 exhibitors from Córdoba, Antioquia, Cesar, La Guajira, Sucre, Putumayo and Magdalena. Weavers raised the growing scarcity of caña flecha and asked for support to grow it locally. The source does not name the organisers; the fair is held in January.

name: Centro Artesanal Corina Urueta
nameEnglish: Corina Urueta Craft Centre (iraca palm weaving)
description: The hub of Usiacurí's iraca palm weaving, in a town where more than 80% of people depend on the craft. Weavers make placemats, bags, earrings and miniature rocking chairs, some coloured with natural pigments.
descriptionOriginal: "En Usiacurí, el arte no solo se aprende: se hereda"; el centro artesanal es el corazón del tejido local en palma de iraca.
details: The June 2025 report profiles weaver Lesbia Jiménez (79, five generations in the craft) and artisan and tour guide Ingris Reales, who leads two productive units of about 50 families. It says the town offers visitor experiences, with murals and colourful streets nearby. Artesanías de Colombia's palm-dyeing ideas are credited with opening new markets. No hours or address are given.

name: Escuela de Artes y Oficios de Galapa
nameEnglish: Galapa School of Arts and Trades
address: Casa de la Cultura de Galapa
description: A free municipal school based at Galapa's Casa de la Cultura, in the town where many of the Barranquilla Carnival's carved masks are made. It teaches wood carving and papier-mâché alongside dance, music and literature.
descriptionOriginal: Creada en 2024, ofrece formación gratuita en talla en madera, papel maché, danza, música y literatura.
details: The school reports more than 800 students from 2024 to 2026. Classes have spread to Villa Olímpica, Mundo Feliz and the corregimiento of Paluato. Mask carver Fernando 'El Mago' Padilla teaches in one of the rooms. The municipality wants to make the school permanent through a municipal agreement. Galapa also holds an annual Festival de la Máscara y el Bejuco; no dates were given.

name: Fernando Padilla "El Mago Padilla"
description: A Galapa carver of Barranquilla Carnival masks and son of master carver Francisco Padilla. He has taught for more than eight years and now teaches at the town's Casa de la Cultura.
descriptionOriginal: Hijo del maestro Francisco Padilla, enseña el oficio de la talla de máscaras desde hace más de ocho años.
details: The craft follows wood treatment, selection and drying, then carving, sanding and painting; Padilla also uses foam (icopor) to make moulds. He teaches through the free Escuela de Artes y Oficios de Galapa. No private workshop address or class schedule is given.

name: Museo Arqueológico de Galapa
description: A small town museum that pairs Galapa's pre-Columbian pottery and ceramics with the contemporary craft of the Carnival mask-makers. Local guides lead visitors through it.
descriptionOriginal: Un espacio donde "se conserva la herencia precolombina" junto a la artesanía contemporánea de Galapa.
details: The February 2025 feature names guides Eider Cera and Luisa Pertuz and says Galapa has more than 220 artisans making masks, costumes and floats for the Barranquilla Carnival. Hours, prices and address were not given.

name: Artecano
description: A family pottery project in the river town of Ponedera, led by Nataly Pertúz De la Cruz with her husband Edwin Mendoza Cano, a third-generation potter. Pieces are thrown on the wheel from local clay, and on weekends the workshop offers immersive sessions where visitors can tread clay barefoot in the mixing pit.
descriptionOriginal: Ofrece talleres inmersivos los fines de semana; los turistas pueden pisar el barro descalzos en la alberca.
details: Makes tableware, interior decor and garden objects, sold in Bogotá, Medellín, Montería, Sincelejo and Santa Marta. The report also mentions Saturday technique classes for about ten local children. It gives no prices, booking contact or address, only that the workshop is a few streets from potter Osman Cano's.

name: Osman Cano (alfarero)
description: A Ponedera potter who works in his patio workshop in a family tradition that came from Mompox. He throws on an old non-electric wheel, fires in a gas kiln and makes tinajas, hen-shaped money boxes, cazuelas and hand-built figures, refusing mass production.
descriptionOriginal: Trabaja en su patio-taller con una tradición familiar llegada desde Mompox; el horno a gas es su única concesión moderna.
details: He also takes in local children at his workshop. The source gives no visit hours or contact, and does not say whether he teaches adult visitors. Ponedera's Cano family are long-standing potters; this entry covers Osman specifically.

name: AMA – Arte Manual Ancestral, Feria Internacional del Caribe
address: Centro de Eventos del Caribe Puerta de Oro, Barranquilla
description: A large curated craft fair for the Colombian Caribbean, created by the Gobernación del Atlántico, for brands and makers who build their work on handcraft. It covers design, decor, art, fashion, wellness and food under the banner 'luxury born of legacy'.
descriptionOriginal: "AMA, Arte Manual Ancestral, es la Gran Feria Artesanal del Caribe", con el lema "Lujo y legado".
details: The second edition ran 14-17 May 2026 at Puerta de Oro, with more than 130 stands and curators including Francesca Miranda. La Guajira's Casa del Artesano was among the exhibitors. At the March 2026 launch, Usiacurí artisans Eblin Vallejo and Ingrid Reales taught guests to weave a palm ring. Exhibitors apply through the website. Later reports of visitor and sales figures were not opened.

name: Artesanías del Atlántico – Tienda principal
nameEnglish: Artesanías del Atlántico flagship craft shop
address: Centro Comercial Plaza Catalunya, local 9, Carrera 58 con Calle 82-60, Barranquilla
description: The Gobernación del Atlántico's flagship craft shop, opened in April 2026, stocking work from more than 23 techniques across the department's towns. Its opening collection mixed home goods and bags in iraca palm, bejuco and enea weaving, carved wood, totumo and clay.
descriptionOriginal: Nueva vitrina del talento artesanal del Atlántico, con piezas "funcionales" y "atemporales".
details: Opened 30 April 2026 by the Secretaría de Cultura y Patrimonio. Open Monday to Saturday, 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. The opening collection, 'Diarios de un Paraíso' (52 items), drew on makers from Piojó, Galapa, Sabanalarga, Usiacurí, Luruaco, Puerto Colombia, Polonuevo, Ponedera, Soledad and Suan.

name: Cooperativa de Artesanos de San Jacinto
description: The artisans' cooperative of San Jacinto, 'tierra de la hamaca grande' in the Montes de María, where hammocks and mochilas are woven on vertical looms of two long wooden posts. Long-time members include Ana Caro and Víctor Mercado, who have woven together in their home patio for more than 55 years.
descriptionOriginal: Tejen en un telar vertical formado por dos maderos largos; Ana: "yo desde los 12 años estoy tejiendo".
details: Ana Caro (80) and Víctor Mercado (82) use coloured cotton threads and a wooden winder, and make hammocks and mochilas. Ana has shown her designs at fairs. The source gives no cooperative address or visiting arrangements. An April 2026 Semana travel piece notes visitors can see the hammock-making process in town; San Jacinto's Festival Nacional Autóctono de Gaitas is in August.

name: Aquí Nació la Hamaca (artesanos de Morroa)
nameEnglish: "The Hammock Was Born Here": Morroa weavers' initiative
description: A collective initiative of Morroa's master weavers to protect, promote and revive hammock-making, the cotton weaving craft at the heart of this Montes de María town. Artisans make hammocks together as a collective.
descriptionOriginal: Iniciativa para "proteger, visibilizar y revitalizar un oficio" que ha marcado la identidad de generaciones.
details: The December 2025 article is brief and names no organisers or workshops. Artesanías de Colombia's directory of artisan organisations (undated listing) shows Morroa hammock groups that can be contacted directly: Grupo Precooperativo Centro Artesanal de Morroa (on the Troncal between Sincelejo and Corozal), Artesanías Rosa María de Morroa (Carrera 5 #4-16) and Artesanos Unidos de Morroa ARTESUM (Calle 6 #7-52, Barrio Chambacú). Whether these groups belong to the initiative was not verified.

name: Asoseynekun
description: A fair-trade-certified Arhuaca association based in Pueblo Bello on the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, grouping about 350 indigenous families who live from coffee, cacao and craft. In 2025 its weavers made the hand-woven cotton mochilas, carrying Sierra Nevada symbols, that the Colombian government gave to foreign leaders.
descriptionOriginal: Asociación con "sede en el municipio de Pueblo Bello, Cesar" que agrupa a "350 familias indígenas".
details: Sixty Arhuaca women from the Yeurua and Cuánime communities wove the government's order, paid at COP 180,000 per mochila. The article gives no public sales channel, contact or visiting information.

name: Eligio Rojas Quintana (orfebre)
description: A Mompox goldsmith known for three-dimensional filigrana momposina pieces, such as scorpions, crabs and tarantulas, that can take two months or more. He trains apprentices in his workshop and has been hired to teach filigree to jewellers in Spain.
descriptionOriginal: "¿Qué hago yo con saber tanto, si no puedo trasmitirlo?"
details: He trained at the Escuela Tomasa Nájera, with an emphasis on goldsmithing, and gained one of 15 places among about 300 applicants at Mompox's Escuela Taller de Artes y Oficios. He then worked in the workshops of masters Luis Ortiz Villanueva and Juan Guzmán, and his work caught the eye of the Spanish brand Tous. His current apprentices include his 15-year-old daughter. Artesanías de Colombia featured him in a filigree demonstration workshop in 2017. The source gives no workshop address and does not say whether he takes outside students.

name: Feria Artesanal y Gastronómica de Semana Santa de Mompox
nameEnglish: Mompox Holy Week Craft and Food Fair
description: A Holy Week craft and food fair in the UNESCO-listed river town of Mompox. It is billed as a major showcase for silver filigrana momposina and regional cooking.
descriptionOriginal: La feria será "un gran escaparate para la filigrana en plata" y los sabores típicos del territorio.
details: Part of the 2026 Holy Week cultural agenda, which ran 29 March to 4 April 2026. The article does not give the fair's exact dates, venue, organisers or exhibitor numbers. It recurs with Holy Week, whose dates change every year.

name: Museo del Oro Tairona – Casa de la Aduana
description: The Banco de la República's free museum in Santa Marta's 18th-century Casa de la Aduana. About 565 objects trace two thousand years of people in the Sierra Nevada and Magdalena, from Tairona and Nahuange archaeological pieces to ethnographic objects.
descriptionOriginal: Con ingreso "totalmente gratuito", exhibe cerca de 565 objetos arqueológicos de la Sierra Nevada y etnográficos del Magdalena.
details: Reopened 19 April 2025 after more than a month of interior repairs and an air-conditioning upgrade. Hours then were 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Sunday 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Guides welcome visitors, and the Sala Bolívar upstairs is where Simón Bolívar lay in state in 1830. In April 2025 it ran guided visits of its tropical-forest tree nursery, linked to the exhibition 'Semillas, memorias que llevan', on timber species used for instruments and ethnographic objects. The Banco de la República cultural site was behind a bot check, so 2026 programming was not verified.

name: Casa Velasco & Cía. (Vidrieras Artísticas de Colombia)
description: A family stained-glass workshop in San Fernando Viejo, founded in the late 1940s by José Velasco Santamaría with master glassmaker Pascual de Ayala y Galán and still run by the family. El País calls it the oldest stained-glass house in Colombia, still working with traditional materials and techniques and training young apprentices.
descriptionOriginal: «Somos de los pocos vitralistas que seguimos trabajando con los materiales y las técnicas artesanales» (Alfonso Velasco, en El País).
details: Current manager: Alfonso Velasco Pardo, the founder's son. The article (June 2025) gives no street address, website or public class or visit programme; it mentions apprentices and calls the workshop a training ground for generations of Colombian stained-glass makers. The founding year is given as 1947 in a caption and 1948 in the text. Ask before visiting.

name: Geominerales Andinos
address: Calle 22A # 9-33, Barrio Obrero, Cali (second outlet: Casa del Bonsai, Km 3 vía La Buitrera)
description: A Cali shop for industrial and garden minerals that also stocks several raw materials a potter can use: natural white kaolin, calcium and sodium bentonite, micronised talc, silica sands and ground brick chamotte (grog). It is mainly a landscaping and bonsai supplier, not a ceramics shop.
descriptionOriginal: Caolín blanco natural: base para esmaltes, lozas y porcelanas de alta calidad.
details: The online store lists the kaolin in 1, 5, 10, 20 and 40 kg sacks from COP 7.000 (the page shows only that one price, the mesh is given as both 150 and 250, and stock was shown as both available and sold out, so confirm before ordering). Micronised talc (mesh 400) is listed from COP 8.000 but is described for farm use, not ceramics. Volume discounts apply. Delivery within Cali and shipping across Colombia; orders over 50 kg by WhatsApp (+57 311 771 2198 or +57 314 296 2523). No feldspar, frits or oxides were found in the catalogue. Confirmed active on its Instagram (@geominerales_cali), October 2026.

name: El Pincel de Marisol, Taller de Arte
description: Marisol Ordóñez's painting and ceramics workshop, with classes in decorative painting and in making ceramics from scratch, group sessions and handmade pieces. The Colombian ceramics collective Entre Grietas lists her as a Cali supplier of high-temperature glazes, watercolour-style high-fire ceramic pigments and slip-casting moulds made to order.
descriptionOriginal: Esmaltes para alta temperatura. Pigmentos cerámicos acuarelables para alta temperatura. Elaboración y venta de moldes para cerámica (moldería).
details: The supplies listing comes from Entre Grietas' supplier directory (page dated 2021), so ask whether glazes, pigments and moulds are still sold. The workshop itself is current: its Google listing shows the Carrera 17 address and phone 300 759 2445, a November 2025 Superprof guide recommends it for painting classes, and it was confirmed active on its Instagram (@elpinceldemarisol, 'Clase de Pintura y Cerámica en Cali'), October 2026. No prices or class schedules could be read.

name: JBerly Art Studio
